title: Incidence realization of a mixed join and replacement of local cocone representatives
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, quasicategories, coherent transformations and cocones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the join-slice comparison $J_a\to P_a$ of [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison]. Let $K$ be a small simplicial set, $I$ a small poset and $(K_i\subseteq K)_{i\in I}$ a monotone family of simplicial subsets. Let $H\subseteq K\star N(I)$ be the mixed subset defined in [lem-coef-directed-cover-mixed-subset-cells]. Define $V_n$ to be the set of pairs $(\sigma,i_0\leq\cdots\leq i_n)$ with $\sigma\in(K_{i_0})_n$. For a monotone map $\theta:[m]\to[n]$, the operator takes this pair to $(\theta^*\sigma,i_{\theta(0)}\leq\cdots\leq i_{\theta(m)})$, using the inclusion $K_{i_0}\subseteq K_{i_{\theta(0)}}$. These sets form a simplicial set $V$. Write $u:V\to K$ and $v:V\to N(I)$ for the two projections, and $v_i:K_i\to V$ for the constant-index map. Let $\mathcal E$ be a quasicategory and $q:H\to\mathcal E$ any simplicial map; put $p=q|_K$ and $c=q|_{N(I)}$.

There is a coherent transformation $a_0:V\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal E$ from $pu$ to $cv$: on $(\sigma,i_0\leq\cdots\leq i_n)$ and a monotone $\epsilon:[n]\to[1]$, apply $q$ to the simplex with initial block $\sigma|_{\epsilon^{-1}(0)}$ and final block $(i_j)_{j\in\epsilon^{-1}(1)}$, retaining the pure block if the other is empty. Its restriction along $v_i\times\mathrm{id}$ is exactly the coherent cocone associated to $q|_{K_i^{\triangleright}}$ by $J_{p|K_i}\to P_{p|K_i}$.

For each $i$, let $\eta_i$ be a prescribed coherent cocone on $p|_{K_i}$ with apex $c(i)$ and choose an equivalence from the preceding associated cocone to $\eta_i$ in the strict fiber of $P_{p|K_i}\to\mathcal E$ over $c(i)$. There exists a coherent transformation $a:V\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal E$ whose endpoints are exactly $pu,cv$ and whose restriction along every $v_i\times\mathrm{id}$ is exactly $\eta_i$. Moreover $a_0$ and $a$ are equivalent as diagrams relative to both endpoints: there is an equivalence edge in the strict fiber of $\operatorname{Fun}(V\times\Delta^1,\mathcal E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(V\times\partial\Delta^1,\mathcal E)$ over the given endpoints, with the chosen local equivalences as restrictions.

For every join cocone $\widetilde\lambda:H^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal E$ on $q$, with apex $C$, let $\lambda$ and $\nu$ be its associated coherent cocones on $p$ and $c$. For any such $a$ and its relative equivalence from $a_0$, there exists a map $t:V\times\Delta^2\to\mathcal E$ with faces $d_2t=a$, $d_0t=(v\times\mathrm{id})^*\nu$ and $d_1t=(u\times\mathrm{id})^*\lambda$. No initiality, colimit, covering, directedness or nonemptiness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of the coherent-transformation meaning of HTT Notation 4.2.3.1 and Proposition 4.2.3.4, printed pp. 248-250, using the comparison of Proposition 4.2.1.5, printed pp. 241-242, and relative equivalence lifting of Corollary 2.4.6.5. The relative replacement and triangle assertion make explicit the fixed-apex representative transport in the original assembly proof. Read online; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this simplicial/quasicategorical comparison.

proof.text: For $\theta:[m]\to[n]$, the proposed operator is defined because $\theta^*\sigma\in(K_{i_0})_m\subseteq(K_{i_{\theta(0)}})_m$. For $\phi:[\ell]\to[m]$, the two successive operators give $((\theta\phi)^*\sigma,i_{\theta\phi(0)}\leq\cdots\leq i_{\theta\phi(\ell)})$, exactly the composite operator; the identity operator is the identity. Thus $V$ is simplicial, and forgetting either coordinate commutes with all operators. Constant index chains likewise give the simplicial maps $v_i$. Their images $W_i$ are simplicial subsets of $V$, and $v_i:K_i\to W_i$ is a degreewise bijection: the first projection recovers the simplex. For $i\ne j$ the constant chains differ in every degree, so $W_i\cap W_j=\varnothing$. Hence $W=\bigcup_iW_i\subseteq V$ is the degreewise disjoint union of the $K_i$, with its specified inclusion. All these sets remain small.

source.place: Agent construction from HTT Notation 4.2.3.1, printed pp. 248-249; check of the incidence operators and constant-index subsets.

proof.text: Define $b:V\times\Delta^1\to H$ by the two-block formula in the statement. If both blocks are nonempty and $r$ is the first position of the final block, the initial block of $\sigma$ lies in $K_{i_0}\subseteq K_{i_r}$, so the resulting mixed simplex lies in $H$ by its cited defining condition. An empty block gives the relevant pure simplex, which also belongs to $H$. Restriction along any monotone map restricts the same two ordered blocks; if one disappears, both descriptions use that same pure summand. Thus the formula commutes with every simplicial operator. At time $0$ it is $u$ into $K$; at time $1$ it is $v$ into $N(I)$. Put $a_0=qb$. For a constant chain at $i$, this is precisely the cylinder-to-join map $K_i\times\Delta^1\to K_i\star\Delta^0$: keep the initial $K_i$ block and repeat the apex in the final block. The explicitly defined fat-to-sharp comparison of the cited join-slice node therefore identifies this restriction with the associated coherent cocone, with literal equality of its simplex formulas.

source.place: Agent two-block calculation for HTT Notation 4.2.3.1 and the explicit comparison of Proposition 4.2.1.5, printed pp. 241 and 248-249.

proof.text: Let $e_i$ be the prescribed edge from $a_0|_{W_i\times\Delta^1}$ to $\eta_i$ in the strict apex fiber. Uncurrying the displayed definition of $P_{p|K_i}$ gives a map $h_i:\Delta^1_s\times K_i\times\Delta^1_t\to\mathcal E$. At $s=0,1$ it is respectively the old cocone and $\eta_i$; at $t=0$ it is $p|_{K_i}$ independently of $s$, and at $t=1$ it is $c(i)$ independently of $s$. Put $B=V\times\Delta^1_t$ and $A=(V\times\partial\Delta^1_t)\cup(W\times\Delta^1_t)\subseteq B$. On $\Delta^1_s\times A$ prescribe the $h_i$ on the disjoint $W_i$ cylinders and the constant homotopy of $pu,cv$ on the two endpoint subsets. Their intersections are exactly $W_i\times\{0,1\}$, where the formulas just computed agree. They therefore define a simplicial map degree by degree. At $s=0$ it agrees with $a_0|_A$, so it glues to $a_0$ on $\{0\}\times B$. Every vertex of $B$ has $t=0$ or $1$ and belongs to $A$; its prescribed $s$-edge is degenerate, hence an equivalence (the doubly degenerate simplex witnesses both inverse equations).

source.place: Agent preparation of the lifting square for Proposition 4.4.5.8 (01NX), using the explicit coherent-comma definition.

proof.text: Apply the cited relative equivalence-prism extension with $\mathcal C=\mathcal E$, $\mathcal D=\Delta^0$, $p$ the unique map, the inclusion $A\subseteq B$ of step 3, and $\epsilon=0$. The terminal simplicial set is a quasicategory, and $\mathcal E\to\Delta^0$ is an inner fibration exactly by the quasicategory horn condition. The inclusion contains all vertices, and all its prescribed vertex edges are equivalences, as verified in step 3. The lower prism map is the unique map to $\Delta^0$. We obtain $h:\Delta^1_s\times B\to\mathcal E$ extending the entire prescribed map, exactly. Set $a=h|_{\{1\}\times B}$. Its endpoint restrictions remain $pu,cv$, and its restriction to $W_i\times\Delta^1_t$ is exactly $\eta_i$. Uncurrying $h$ gives an edge from $a_0$ to $a$ in the strict fixed-endpoint fiber, whose restrictions are the chosen edges $e_i$, not merely their homotopy classes.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.5.8 (01NX), opposite orientation epsilon=0, with target the point.

proof.text: Apply the cited fixed-boundary Kan theorem to $B=V\times\Delta^1$, $A_0=V\times\partial\Delta^1$, $X=\mathcal E$ and the endpoint map $f=(pu,cv)$. The subset $A_0$ contains all vertices, so the exact strict fiber in the statement is a Kan complex $Z$. The edge $h$ of step 4 lies in $Z$. For completeness, every edge $e:x\to y$ of a Kan complex has inverse triangles: fill $\Lambda^2_0$ with edges $01=e$ and $02=1_x$, obtaining $f:y\to x$ and a triangle with edges $(e,f,1_x)$. Then fill $\Lambda^3_0$ on vertices $(x,y,x,y)$, with face $012$ that triangle, face $023$ the degeneracy of $e$ with edges $(1_x,e,e)$, and face $013$ its other degeneracy with edges $(e,1_y,e)$. These three faces agree on overlaps; the missing face $123$ has edges $(f,e,1_y)$. These are exactly the two inverse witnesses required by the definition of equivalence. Apply this within $Z$ to $h$. Thus $h$ is the required equivalence relative to both endpoints, with all chosen local restrictions.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.1.11 (01P1); the final two horn fillings unpack the definition of equivalence in a Kan complex.

proof.text: Given $\widetilde\lambda:H\star\Delta^0\to\mathcal E$, define $r:V\times\Delta^2\to H\star\Delta^0$ as follows. For $(\sigma,i_0\leq\cdots\leq i_n)$ and $\rho:[n]\to[2]$, use the restriction of $\sigma$ on $\rho^{-1}(0)$, the index chain on $\rho^{-1}(1)$, and the repeated final apex on $\rho^{-1}(2)$, in that order; omit empty blocks. The first two nonempty blocks concatenate to an $H$ simplex: if both occur, the first lies in $K_{i_0}\subseteq K_{i_j}$ for the first index $j$ of the second block. If only one occurs it is a pure simplex of $H$. Append the third block by the defining ordered-join formula; if the first two are empty, use the pure apex simplex. Under any simplicial operator, the three blocks are restricted in order, including the cases where a block disappears. This gives the same formula after restriction, so $r$ is simplicial. Put $t_0=\widetilde\lambda r$. Its $01$ face is $a_0$ by step 2. Its $12$ face keeps the index block followed by the apex and is therefore $(v\times\mathrm{id})^*\nu$. Its $02$ face keeps the $K$ block followed by the apex and is $(u\times\mathrm{id})^*\lambda$. Both equalities are exactly the cylinder formulas defining the associated cocones under the cited join-slice comparison, in every degree.

source.place: Agent three-block calculation from the ordered join of HTT Notation 4.2.3.1 and the cylinder comparison of Proposition 4.2.1.5.

proof.text: Now take any $a$ and any specified relative equivalence from $a_0$ to $a$ as in the statement, not necessarily the one constructed above. Its underlying edge uncurries to $e:\Delta^1_s\times V\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal E$, with $s$-ends $a_0,a$, constant in $s$ at the two endpoints of the last factor. Let $B'=V\times\Delta^2$ and $A'=V\times\partial\Delta^2$. On $\Delta^1_s\times A'$ prescribe $e$ on edge $01$, the constant homotopy of $(v\times\mathrm{id})^*\nu$ on edge $12$, and the constant homotopy of $(u\times\mathrm{id})^*\lambda$ on edge $02$. At their pairwise intersections (the three vertices of the triangle) the maps agree: they are respectively $pu$, $cv$, and the constant diagram at $C$, independently of $s$. Hence they glue degree by degree to a simplicial map, and at $s=0$ agree with $t_0|_{A'}$ by step 6. Every vertex of $B'$ lies in $A'$, and every prescribed $s$-edge at a vertex is degenerate.

source.place: Agent boundary preparation for Proposition 4.4.5.8 (01NX); agreement at all three corners is explicit.

proof.text: Apply the relative equivalence-prism extension again, with inclusion $A'\subseteq B'$, $\epsilon=0$, $\mathcal E\to\Delta^0$, the boundary homotopy of step 7, and $t_0$ on $\{0\}\times B'$. The quasicategory and inner-fibration conditions are the same as in step 4; $A'$ contains all vertices, and the prescribed vertex edges are degenerate equivalences. The extension $T:\Delta^1_s\times B'\to\mathcal E$ therefore exists and preserves the entire boundary homotopy exactly. Its $s=1$ restriction $t$ has faces $d_2t=a$, $d_0t=(v\times\mathrm{id})^*\nu$ and $d_1t=(u\times\mathrm{id})^*\lambda$, by those boundary prescriptions. No use was made of initiality, colimits, directedness or covering. If $I$ or $V$ is empty the maps with source $V$ are the unique empty maps; if $\mathcal E$ is empty, existence of $q$ already forces its source empty. Thus the stated empty cases are included without an extra hypothesis.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.5.8 (01NX), epsilon=0, applied to the full triangle boundary.
